seo.title: How to Build a Full-Stack App with Supabase | Full Stack Guide
seo.description: Build a full-stack app with Next.js and Supabase covering authentication, database queries, realtime subscriptions, and file storage in one guide.

introduction: Supabase replaces your entire backend with a Postgres database, auth system, realtime engine, and file storage — all accessible through a typed client library. Instead of stitching together Firebase, Auth0, and S3, you get one SDK and one dashboard. This guide builds a full-stack task management app with Next.js that uses every major Supabase feature.

prerequisites.name: Node.js 20+
prerequisites.description: Required for Next.js 15 with the App Router and server components.

prerequisites.name: Supabase Account
prerequisites.description: Create a free Supabase project to get a Postgres database, auth, realtime, and storage out of the box.

prerequisites.name: Supabase CLI
prerequisites.description: The Supabase CLI lets you run migrations, generate types, and test locally before deploying.

prerequisites.name: Basic SQL Knowledge
prerequisites.description: Familiarity with CREATE TABLE, SELECT, INSERT, and JOIN queries. Supabase is Postgres, so standard SQL applies.

steps.title: Scaffold Next.js and Install the Supabase Client
steps.description: Create a Next.js app and install the Supabase client libraries. The @supabase/ssr package handles cookie-based auth sessions for server components and middleware. Generate TypeScript types from your database schema so every query is type-safe.

code_snippet.code:
npx create-next-app@latest taskflow --typescript --tailwind --app --src-dir
cd taskflow

npm install @supabase/supabase-js @supabase/ssr

# Initialize Supabase locally
npx supabase init
npx supabase start

# Generate types from your database schema
npx supabase gen types typescript --local > src/lib/database.types.ts

tips: Run 'npx supabase start' to get a local Postgres + Auth + Storage instance for development — no cloud project needed.
Regenerate types after every migration with 'supabase gen types typescript' to keep your client type-safe.

steps.title: Create the Database Schema with Row-Level Security
steps.description: Define your tables and enable Row-Level Security (RLS) so each user can only access their own data. RLS policies run at the Postgres level — even if your app code has a bug, unauthorized data access is impossible. Write a migration that creates the projects and tasks tables with foreign keys and policies.
tips: Always enable RLS on every table — tables without RLS are publicly accessible through the Supabase API.
Use auth.uid() in policies to reference the currently authenticated user's ID.

steps.title: Set Up Authentication with Server-Side Sessions
steps.description: Configure the Supabase client for both server and client components. The server client reads the auth session from cookies, while the client-side instance handles login and sign-up flows. Create utility functions that return the correct client for each context.
tips: Pass the Database generic to createServerClient for end-to-end type safety on all queries.
The server client wraps Next.js cookies() so Supabase auth works seamlessly with server components and middleware.

steps.title: Build CRUD Operations with Type-Safe Queries
steps.description: Create server actions for creating, reading, updating, and deleting tasks. Supabase's query builder chains like Prisma but runs directly against Postgres. Because RLS is enabled, you don't need to filter by user_id in your queries — the policy handles authorization automatically.
tips: Use revalidatePath after mutations to update server component data without a full page reload.
Supabase returns typed data based on your Database type — hover over query results to see the exact shape.

steps.title: Add Realtime Subscriptions for Live Updates
steps.description: Subscribe to database changes so the UI updates instantly when tasks are created, updated, or deleted — even by other users on the same project. Supabase's Realtime engine uses WebSockets and Postgres logical replication. The client subscribes to a channel scoped to a specific project's tasks.
tips: Enable Realtime for specific tables in the Supabase Dashboard under Database > Replication.
Always clean up channels in the useEffect return function to prevent memory leaks and duplicate subscriptions.

steps.title: Add File Storage for Task Attachments
steps.description: Use Supabase Storage to let users upload file attachments to tasks. Storage uses the same RLS-style policies as your database, so files are access-controlled per user. Create a storage bucket with upload limits and a server action that handles the file upload and links it to a task.
tips: Set storage policies in SQL: create policy on storage.objects using (auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]).
Use upsert: false to prevent overwriting existing files — append a timestamp to filenames for uniqueness.

steps.title: Deploy to Vercel with Supabase Integration
steps.description: Deploy your Next.js app to Vercel and connect it to your Supabase cloud project. Vercel's Supabase integration automatically syncs environment variables. Run your migrations against the production database and configure auth redirect URLs for your production domain.

code_snippet.code:
# Link to your Supabase cloud project
npx supabase link --project-ref YOUR_PROJECT_REF

# Push migrations to production
npx supabase db push

# Generate types from production schema
npx supabase gen types typescript --linked > src/lib/database.types.ts

# Deploy to Vercel
npm install -g vercel
vercel
vercel env add NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
vercel env add NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
vercel --prod

tips: Add your Vercel deployment URL to Supabase Auth > URL Configuration > Redirect URLs.
Use 'supabase db push' for initial deploys and 'supabase db reset' to replay all migrations from scratch locally.
Enable Supabase's built-in Postgres backups (point-in-time recovery) on the Pro plan for production.
